# Circuit Séance — Requirements

**Feature:** Circuit Séance MVP  
**Hackathon:** Kiroween 2026 — "Resurrection" category  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** 2026-11-02

---

## Overview

Circuit Séance (电路招魂) is a fully client-side browser application that lets EE students photograph or upload a hand-drawn schematic, transcribe it to SPICE via a vision LLM, simulate it in-browser with ngspice/WebAssembly, display results on a haunted green-phosphor CRT oscilloscope, and receive an AI "spirit" explanation of the waveform. Bundled example circuits make the app fully usable with no API key.

---

## User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Project Bootstrap & Shell

**1.1** As a developer, I need a Vite + React 18 + TypeScript strict-mode project with all tooling configured so the team has a working build baseline.

- WHEN a developer runs `npm run dev` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL start a Vite dev server that serves the app without errors.
- WHEN a developer runs `npm run build` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a production-ready static bundle in `dist/` without TypeScript errors.
- WHEN a developer runs `npm run lint` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL check ESLint and Prettier rules and exit non-zero on violations.
- WHEN a developer runs `npm test` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL run Vitest in single-run mode and report pass/fail.
- WHERE TypeScript `strict: true` is set, THE SYSTEM SHALL reject any `any` type without an explanatory comment.

**1.2** As a user, I need a bilingual (English / Simplified Chinese) UI so I can use the app in my preferred language.

- WHEN the user selects Simplified Chinese in the language toggle THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display all UI labels, buttons, error messages, and help text in Simplified Chinese.
- WHEN the user selects English THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display all text in English.
- IF no explicit language has been selected THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL default to English.
- WHEN THE SYSTEM renders any text element THEN it SHALL use the string from the active i18n locale file (`en.ts` or `zh-CN.ts`), not hardcoded literals.

---

### 2. Example Circuits

**2.1** As a user with no API key, I need bundled example circuits so I can experience the full simulation loop without configuring any LLM.

- WHEN the user opens the app for the first time THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a list of at least six bundled example circuits: RC low-pass filter, RL circuit, RLC ringing, diode rectifier, BJT common-emitter amplifier, and op-amp inverting amplifier.
- WHEN the user selects an example circuit THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL load its netlist into the netlist editor without requiring any API key or network call.
- WHEN an example circuit is loaded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL automatically run the simulation for that circuit and display results on the oscilloscope.
- WHERE an example circuit is active and no API key is configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a rule-based offline explanation instead of calling the LLM spirit.

**2.2** As a developer, I need each example circuit stored as a plain-text `.net` file in `src/examples/` so they can be bundled by Vite and updated independently.

- WHEN the project is built THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include all `.net` files from `src/examples/` in the bundle and make them importable as strings.

---

### 3. Netlist Editor & Validation

**3.1** As a user, I need a syntax-highlighted SPICE netlist editor so I can read and edit netlists with clear visual feedback.

- WHEN the netlist editor is rendered THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use CodeMirror 6 with a custom SPICE syntax mode covering: component lines (R, C, L, V, I, D, Q, M, E, F, G, H, X), `.tran`, `.ac`, `.dc`, `.op` directives, `.model`, `.subckt`, and comments (`;` and `*`).
- WHEN the user types in the netlist editor THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL apply syntax highlighting in real time.
- WHEN the editor contains a line flagged as erroneous by validation THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL highlight that line with a visual marker (gutter icon or underline) distinct from the phosphor-green syntax colour.

**3.2** As a user, I need the netlist validated before simulation so broken circuits produce clear error messages instead of cryptic WASM failures.

- WHEN the user requests simulation THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL first run a syntax validation pass (parse) over the netlist; IF it finds unrecognised lines or missing required directives THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display the specific errors and SHALL NOT start the simulation.
- WHEN the syntax validation passes THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL run an element/node check (at least: no floating nodes, ground node 0 present, all referenced models defined).
- WHEN the element/node check passes THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL submit the netlist to the Web Worker for an ngspice dry run; IF ngspice returns an error THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL surface a human-readable "spirits are restless" message that includes the raw ngspice error in a collapsible detail section.
- WHEN all three validation stages pass THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL proceed to full simulation.
- WHEN validation identifies a problem line THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL scroll the editor to that line and apply an error marker.

**3.3** As a user, I need to paste or type a netlist directly so I can use the app as a quick netlist runner without a schematic image.

- WHEN the user clears the editor and types a netlist manually THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL treat it identically to a loaded example or LLM-transcribed netlist for the purposes of validation and simulation.

---

### 4. Simulation Engine (Web Worker)

**4.1** As a user, I need in-browser ngspice simulation so I can get results without any server or internet connection.

- WHEN the simulation is initiated THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL run `eecircuit-engine` exclusively inside a Web Worker so THE UI thread is never blocked.
- WHEN the Web Worker starts for the first time THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL lazy-load the ~40 MB WASM package; once loaded, THE SYSTEM SHALL cache it so subsequent simulations do not re-fetch it.
- WHILE the WASM package is loading THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a "Summoning…" loading indicator on the oscilloscope screen.
- WHEN `sim.runSim()` resolves THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL transfer the `SimResult` back to the main thread via structured clone.

**4.2** As a user, I need the simulation to handle errors gracefully so I learn what to fix rather than seeing a blank screen.

- WHEN ngspice returns an error (e.g. singular matrix, timestep too small, missing ground) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL catch it in the Worker, translate it to a `SimError` message, and post it to the main thread.
- WHEN the main thread receives a `SimError` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a "The spirits are restless" panel with a friendly short message, the raw ngspice error in a `<details>` block, and optionally a spirit-suggested fix if the error pattern is recognisable (e.g. "Add a ground node 0 to anchor your circuit.").
- IF the spirit key is configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL offer to ask the spirit for a fix suggestion automatically.

**4.3** As a developer, I need a typed Worker message protocol so the main thread and worker communicate safely.

- WHEN the main thread posts a `SimulateRequest` message THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include the fields: `type: 'simulate'`, `netlist: string`, `id: string`.
- WHEN the Worker posts a success response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateResponse` with fields: `type: 'result'`, `id: string`, `result: SimResult`.
- WHEN the Worker posts an error response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateError` with fields: `type: 'error'`, `id: string`, `message: string`, `raw: string`.
- WHEN the Worker posts a progress update THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateProgress` with fields: `type: 'progress'`, `id: string`, `stage: 'loading' | 'running'`.

---

### 5. CRT Oscilloscope Display

**5.1** As a user, I need a green-phosphor CRT oscilloscope display so simulation results feel authentic and visually distinctive.

- WHEN a simulation result is available THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render the output on an HTML Canvas 2D element styled to look like a P31 green-phosphor CRT oscilloscope.
- WHEN rendering traces THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL apply: phosphor glow/bloom effect, persistence/afterglow trails that decay over ~0.5 s, subtle scanline overlay, and a low-frequency brightness flicker effect.
- WHEN `prefers-reduced-motion` is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL disable the flicker and afterglow animations and render a static trace with glow only.
- WHEN rendering text labels (axis labels, voltage/time values) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (≥ 4.5:1) against the dark CRT background.
- WHEN a simulation result with ≤ 10 000 data points is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop without dropped frames.

**5.2** As a user, I need a graticule and channel controls so I can read waveform values accurately.

- WHEN the oscilloscope is rendered THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL draw a graticule of 10 × 8 divisions with tick marks and centre-line subdivisions.
- WHEN a transient simulation result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show time on the x-axis and allow the user to select up to 4 probe signals from the simulation output variables as channels.
- WHEN an AC simulation result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display Bode magnitude (dB) and phase (degrees) on a log-frequency x-axis.
- WHEN a DC sweep result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display the sweep variable on the x-axis and the output variable on the y-axis.
- WHEN an operating-point result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a node-voltage readout panel (table of node names and DC voltages) instead of a waveform canvas.
- WHEN the oscilloscope is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL provide volts/div and time/div (or freq/div for AC) controls that rescale the trace in real time.
- WHEN the user changes the channel or div controls THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL update the display within one animation frame.

**5.3** As a user on a mobile phone, I want the oscilloscope to be usable in landscape orientation so I can capture circuits with the camera and still read the scope.

- WHEN the viewport width is < 768 px and orientation is landscape THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render the scope canvas full-width and stack controls below.
- WHEN the viewport width is < 768 px THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL make all interactive controls (knobs, channel selectors) large enough to tap accurately (minimum 44 × 44 px touch target per WCAG 2.5.5).

---

### 6. Image Capture & Upload

**6.1** As a student, I need to photograph my hand-drawn schematic with my phone camera so I can transcribe it without retyping.

- WHEN the user taps the "Capture" button on a mobile device THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL open the device camera via `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">`.
- WHEN the user selects "Upload" THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL open a standard file picker accepting `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, and `image/gif`.
- WHEN an image is selected or captured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a preview of the image in the capture panel.
- WHEN an image exceeds 5 MB THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL resize/compress it client-side to ≤ 5 MB before sending to the LLM.
- IF the browser does not support the File API THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an unsupported-feature warning.

---

### 7. Vision LLM Transcription

**7.1** As a user, I need the app to convert my schematic photo to a SPICE netlist using a vision LLM so I don't have to write SPICE by hand.

- WHEN the user clicks "Transcribe" with an image loaded and an API key configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL call `LLMAdapter.transcribeSchematic(imageBase64, mimeType)` and display a loading indicator.
- WHEN the LLM returns a response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL extract the netlist from within a fenced code block (`` ```spice `` or `` ``` ``), and SHALL also capture any confidence/caveat note the model appended.
- WHEN the extracted netlist is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show it side-by-side with the original schematic photo (two-pane layout).
- WHEN the transcription completes THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL automatically run the three-stage validation on the returned netlist and display any errors in the editor.
- IF no fenced code block is found in the LLM response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an error "The spirit could not read the circuit" and prompt the user to retry or enter the netlist manually.
- WHEN the LLM call fails (network error, auth error, rate limit) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a specific error message indicating the failure type and SHALL NOT overwrite any existing netlist in the editor.

**7.2** As a user, I need to configure my LLM provider and API key so I control which service is used and my key stays private.

- WHEN the user opens the Settings panel THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL present a choice of provider: "OpenAI-compatible" or "Anthropic Claude".
- WHEN "OpenAI-compatible" is selected THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a configurable base URL field (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`) and an API key field.
- WHEN "Anthropic Claude" is selected THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an API key field.
- WHEN the user saves an API key THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL store it in `localStorage` (with an opt-in "remember" toggle defaulting to `sessionStorage`) and SHALL NEVER transmit it to any server except the user-chosen provider endpoint.
- WHEN an API key is stored THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display it masked (e.g. `sk-…abc4`) in the settings UI.
- WHEN no API key is configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL disable the "Transcribe" and "Ask Spirit" buttons and display a prompt to configure a key.

**7.3** As a developer, I need a provider-agnostic LLM adapter interface so new providers can be added without modifying feature code.

- WHEN any feature calls the LLM THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL do so through the `LLMAdapter` interface (`transcribeSchematic` and `explainWaveform` methods only); it SHALL NOT import provider-specific code directly.
- WHEN the OpenAI-compatible adapter is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL construct a chat-completions request with a base64-encoded image in the `image_url` content part and the model name configurable by the user.
- WHEN the Anthropic adapter is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use the Anthropic Messages API with the image in a `image` content block.
- WHEN either adapter receives an HTTP error response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL throw a typed `LLMError` with `provider`, `statusCode`, and `message` fields.

---

### 8. AI Spirit — Waveform Explanation

**8.1** As a user, I need the AI spirit to explain my simulation results in plain language so I understand what the waveform shows.

- WHEN the user clicks "Ask the Spirit" after a successful simulation THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL call `LLMAdapter.explainWaveform(netlist, compactSummary)` where `compactSummary` contains the analysis type and numeric digest (see §8.2), NOT raw data arrays.
- WHEN the spirit response arrives THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render it as formatted Markdown in the spirit panel, including the suggested "try next" experiment.
- WHEN the UI language is Simplified Chinese THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL instruct the LLM adapter to request a Simplified Chinese explanation.
- WHEN THE SYSTEM calls explainWaveform THEN it SHALL include in the prompt: netlist text, analysis type, and the compact numeric summary.

**8.2** As a developer, I need a result summariser that compresses `SimResult` to a compact numeric digest so LLM prompts stay small.

- WHEN a transient result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL compute and include: min, max, and final value per channel; estimated time constant (τ from 63.2% rise); rise time (10%–90%); percentage overshoot if present.
- WHEN an AC result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: –3 dB frequency, DC gain (dB), peak gain (dB) and frequency if present.
- WHEN a DC sweep result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: min/max output, slope at mid-point.
- WHEN an operating-point result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: all node voltages as key-value pairs.
- WHEN the summary is computed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL cap it at 500 tokens (approximately 2 000 characters) by truncating the least significant digits.

**8.3** As a user with no API key, I need an offline spirit explanation for the bundled examples so the "Resurrection" narrative is complete even without an LLM.

- WHEN an example circuit is active AND no API key is set AND the user clicks "Ask the Spirit" THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a pre-written, rule-based explanation for that example, formatted identically to a live LLM explanation.
- WHERE a rule-based explanation is shown THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a small "offline mode" badge so the user knows it is pre-written.

---

### 9. Application Shell & Settings

**9.1** As a user, I need a coherent single-page layout so all features are accessible without confusing navigation.

- WHEN the app loads THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display: a top toolbar (app title, language toggle, settings icon); a main area split into a left panel (capture/netlist) and a right panel (oscilloscope + spirit); and a status bar.
- WHEN the viewport is < 1024 px wide THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL collapse the split layout into a single-column stacked layout with the capture/netlist panel above the scope panel.
- WHEN the app is loaded on a mobile browser THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL be usable for the full core loop (capture → simulate → scope) within a single scroll.

**9.2** As a developer, I need the app to be deployable as a static site so there is no hosting infrastructure to manage.

- WHEN `npm run build` is run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a `dist/` directory containing only static files (HTML, JS, CSS, WASM, assets) with no server-side code.
- WHEN the static files are served from any CDN or static host (GitHub Pages, Vercel, Netlify) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL function without any back-end.

---

### 10. Accessibility & Performance

**10.1** As a user with accessibility needs, I need the app to respect motion preferences and maintain readable contrast.

- WHEN `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL suppress all CSS animations, canvas flicker, and phosphor persistence animation.
- WHERE any text is rendered over a background THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain ≥ 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG AA).
- WHEN the user interacts with the app using a keyboard only THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL support focus traversal of all primary controls (tab order, visible focus ring).
- WHEN any button or icon-only control exists THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL provide an accessible label (`aria-label` or visible label text).

**10.2** As a user, I need fast initial load and smooth runtime performance.

- WHEN the app is first loaded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a usable shell (title, example list, empty scope) within 3 seconds on a broadband connection before WASM is fetched.
- WHEN the WASM engine is not yet loaded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show a progress/loading state; it SHALL NOT block rendering of the rest of the UI.
- WHEN rendering a simulation result of ≤ 10 000 points THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL sustain 60 fps on the scope canvas.

---

### 11. Testing

**11.1** As a developer, I need unit tests for the netlist parser and validator so regressions are caught automatically.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that the netlist parser correctly identifies component types, node names, and directive parameters for at least 20 representative netlist lines.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that the validator correctly accepts valid netlists and rejects netlists with: missing ground, floating nodes, unrecognised directives, and malformed component lines.
- WHEN property tests (fast-check) are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify the parser round-trip property: `serialise(parse(netlist)) === normalise(netlist)` for arbitrary well-formed netlists.

**11.2** As a developer, I need a unit test for the result summariser so its numeric outputs are correct.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that summarising a known transient result produces the correct τ, rise time, overshoot, min, max, and final values within ±1% tolerance.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that summarising a known AC result produces the correct –3 dB frequency within ±0.5 dB tolerance.

**11.3** As a developer, I need a unit test for LLM response parsing so malformed model outputs are handled gracefully.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that a response containing a fenced code block yields the correct netlist string.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that a response with no fenced block returns a typed parse error rather than throwing.

**11.4** As a developer, I need one end-to-end smoke test so the critical happy path is validated in a real browser.

- WHEN the Playwright smoke test runs THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL: load the app, select the RC low-pass example, wait for the simulation to complete, and assert that a canvas element with a non-blank trace is visible on screen.

</content>

- WHEN the Web Worker starts for the first time THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL lazy-load the ~40 MB WASM package; once loaded, THE SYSTEM SHALL cache it so subsequent simulations do not re-fetch it.
- WHILE the WASM package is loading THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a "Summoning…" loading indicator on the oscilloscope screen.
- WHEN `sim.runSim()` resolves THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL transfer the `SimResult` back to the main thread via structured clone.

**4.2** As a user, I need the simulation to handle errors gracefully so I learn what to fix rather than seeing a blank screen.

- WHEN ngspice returns an error (e.g. singular matrix, timestep too small, missing ground) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL catch it in the Worker, translate it to a `SimError` message, and post it to the main thread.
- WHEN the main thread receives a `SimError` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a "The spirits are restless" panel with a friendly short message, the raw ngspice error in a `<details>` block, and optionally a spirit-suggested fix if the error pattern is recognisable (e.g. "Add a ground node 0 to anchor your circuit.").
- IF the spirit key is configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL offer to ask the spirit for a fix suggestion automatically.

**4.3** As a developer, I need a typed Worker message protocol so the main thread and worker communicate safely.

- WHEN the main thread posts a `SimulateRequest` message THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include the fields: `type: 'simulate'`, `netlist: string`, `id: string`.
- WHEN the Worker posts a success response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateResponse` with fields: `type: 'result'`, `id: string`, `result: SimResult`.
- WHEN the Worker posts an error response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateError` with fields: `type: 'error'`, `id: string`, `message: string`, `raw: string`.
- WHEN the Worker posts a progress update THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use type `SimulateProgress` with fields: `type: 'progress'`, `id: string`, `stage: 'loading' | 'running'`.

---

### 5. CRT Oscilloscope Display

**5.1** As a user, I need a green-phosphor CRT oscilloscope display so simulation results feel authentic and visually distinctive.

- WHEN a simulation result is available THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render the output on an HTML Canvas 2D element styled to look like a P31 green-phosphor CRT oscilloscope.
- WHEN rendering traces THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL apply: phosphor glow/bloom effect, persistence/afterglow trails that decay over ~0.5 s, subtle scanline overlay, and a low-frequency brightness flicker effect.
- WHEN `prefers-reduced-motion` is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL disable the flicker and afterglow animations and render a static trace with glow only.
- WHEN rendering text labels (axis labels, voltage/time values) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (≥ 4.5:1) against the dark CRT background.
- WHEN a simulation result with ≤ 10 000 data points is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render at 60 fps on a mid-range laptop without dropped frames.

**5.2** As a user, I need a graticule and channel controls so I can read waveform values accurately.

- WHEN the oscilloscope is rendered THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL draw a graticule of 10 × 8 divisions with tick marks and centre-line subdivisions.
- WHEN a transient simulation result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show time on the x-axis and allow the user to select up to 4 probe signals from the simulation output variables as channels.
- WHEN an AC simulation result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display Bode magnitude (dB) and phase (degrees) on a log-frequency x-axis.
- WHEN a DC sweep result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display the sweep variable on the x-axis and the output variable on the y-axis.
- WHEN an operating-point result is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a node-voltage readout panel (table of node names and DC voltages) instead of a waveform canvas.
- WHEN the oscilloscope is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL provide volts/div and time/div (or freq/div for AC) controls that rescale the trace in real time.
- WHEN the user changes the channel or div controls THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL update the display within one animation frame.

**5.3** As a user on a mobile phone, I want the oscilloscope to be usable in landscape orientation so I can capture circuits with the camera and still read the scope.

- WHEN the viewport width is < 768 px and orientation is landscape THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render the scope canvas full-width and stack controls below.
- WHEN the viewport width is < 768 px THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL make all interactive controls (knobs, channel selectors) large enough to tap accurately (minimum 44 × 44 px touch target per WCAG 2.5.5).

---

### 6. Image Capture & Upload

**6.1** As a student, I need to photograph my hand-drawn schematic with my phone camera so I can transcribe it without retyping.

- WHEN the user taps the "Capture" button on a mobile device THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL open the device camera via `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">`.
- WHEN the user selects "Upload" THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL open a standard file picker accepting `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, and `image/gif`.
- WHEN an image is selected or captured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a preview of the image in the capture panel.
- WHEN an image exceeds 5 MB THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL resize/compress it client-side to ≤ 5 MB before sending to the LLM.
- IF the browser does not support the File API THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an unsupported-feature warning.

---

### 7. Vision LLM Transcription

**7.1** As a user, I need the app to convert my schematic photo to a SPICE netlist using a vision LLM so I don't have to write SPICE by hand.

- WHEN the user clicks "Transcribe" with an image loaded and an API key configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL call `LLMAdapter.transcribeSchematic(imageBase64, mimeType)` and display a loading indicator.
- WHEN the LLM returns a response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL extract the netlist from within a fenced code block (`` ```spice `` or `` ``` ``), and SHALL also capture any confidence/caveat note the model appended.
- WHEN the extracted netlist is displayed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show it side-by-side with the original schematic photo (two-pane layout).
- WHEN the transcription completes THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL automatically run the three-stage validation on the returned netlist and display any errors in the editor.
- IF no fenced code block is found in the LLM response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an error "The spirit could not read the circuit" and prompt the user to retry or enter the netlist manually.
- WHEN the LLM call fails (network error, auth error, rate limit) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a specific error message indicating the failure type and SHALL NOT overwrite any existing netlist in the editor.

**7.2** As a user, I need to configure my LLM provider and API key so I control which service is used and my key stays private.

- WHEN the user opens the Settings panel THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL present a choice of provider: "OpenAI-compatible" or "Anthropic Claude".
- WHEN "OpenAI-compatible" is selected THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a configurable base URL field (default `https://api.openai.com/v1`) and an API key field.
- WHEN "Anthropic Claude" is selected THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display an API key field.
- WHEN the user saves an API key THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL store it in `localStorage` (with an opt-in "remember" toggle defaulting to `sessionStorage`) and SHALL NEVER transmit it to any server except the user-chosen provider endpoint.
- WHEN an API key is stored THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display it masked (e.g. `sk-…abc4`) in the settings UI.
- WHEN no API key is configured THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL disable the "Transcribe" and "Ask Spirit" buttons and display a prompt to configure a key.

**7.3** As a developer, I need a provider-agnostic LLM adapter interface so new providers can be added without modifying feature code.

- WHEN any feature calls the LLM THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL do so through the `LLMAdapter` interface (`transcribeSchematic` and `explainWaveform` methods only); it SHALL NOT import provider-specific code directly.
- WHEN the OpenAI-compatible adapter is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL construct a chat-completions request with a base64-encoded image in the `image_url` content part and the model name configurable by the user.
- WHEN the Anthropic adapter is active THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL use the Anthropic Messages API with the image in a `image` content block.
- WHEN either adapter receives an HTTP error response THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL throw a typed `LLMError` with `provider`, `statusCode`, and `message` fields.

---

### 8. AI Spirit — Waveform Explanation

**8.1** As a user, I need the AI spirit to explain my simulation results in plain language so I understand what the waveform shows.

- WHEN the user clicks "Ask the Spirit" after a successful simulation THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL call `LLMAdapter.explainWaveform(netlist, compactSummary)` where `compactSummary` contains the analysis type and numeric digest (see §8.2), NOT raw data arrays.
- WHEN the spirit response arrives THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL render it as formatted Markdown in the spirit panel, including the suggested "try next" experiment.
- WHEN the UI language is Simplified Chinese THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL instruct the LLM adapter to request a Simplified Chinese explanation.
- WHEN THE SYSTEM calls explainWaveform THEN it SHALL include in the prompt: netlist text, analysis type, and the compact numeric summary.

**8.2** As a developer, I need a result summariser that compresses `SimResult` to a compact numeric digest so LLM prompts stay small.

- WHEN a transient result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL compute and include: min, max, and final value per channel; estimated time constant (τ from 63.2% rise); rise time (10%–90%); percentage overshoot if present.
- WHEN an AC result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: –3 dB frequency, DC gain (dB), peak gain (dB) and frequency if present.
- WHEN a DC sweep result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: min/max output, slope at mid-point.
- WHEN an operating-point result is summarised THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL include: all node voltages as key-value pairs.
- WHEN the summary is computed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL cap it at 500 tokens (approximately 2 000 characters) by truncating the least significant digits.

**8.3** As a user with no API key, I need an offline spirit explanation for the bundled examples so the "Resurrection" narrative is complete even without an LLM.

- WHEN an example circuit is active AND no API key is set AND the user clicks "Ask the Spirit" THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a pre-written, rule-based explanation for that example, formatted identically to a live LLM explanation.
- WHERE a rule-based explanation is shown THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a small "offline mode" badge so the user knows it is pre-written.

---

### 9. Application Shell & Settings

**9.1** As a user, I need a coherent single-page layout so all features are accessible without confusing navigation.

- WHEN the app loads THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display: a top toolbar (app title, language toggle, settings icon); a main area split into a left panel (capture/netlist) and a right panel (oscilloscope + spirit); and a status bar.
- WHEN the viewport is < 1024 px wide THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL collapse the split layout into a single-column stacked layout with the capture/netlist panel above the scope panel.
- WHEN the app is loaded on a mobile browser THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL be usable for the full core loop (capture → simulate → scope) within a single scroll.

**9.2** As a developer, I need the app to be deployable as a static site so there is no hosting infrastructure to manage.

- WHEN `npm run build` is run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a `dist/` directory containing only static files (HTML, JS, CSS, WASM, assets) with no server-side code.
- WHEN the static files are served from any CDN or static host (GitHub Pages, Vercel, Netlify) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL function without any back-end.

---

### 10. Accessibility & Performance

**10.1** As a user with accessibility needs, I need the app to respect motion preferences and maintain readable contrast.

- WHEN `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL suppress all CSS animations, canvas flicker, and phosphor persistence animation.
- WHERE any text is rendered over a background THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain ≥ 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG AA).
- WHEN the user interacts with the app using a keyboard only THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL support focus traversal of all primary controls (tab order, visible focus ring).
- WHEN any button or icon-only control exists THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL provide an accessible label (`aria-label` or visible label text).

**10.2** As a user, I need fast initial load and smooth runtime performance.

- WHEN the app is first loaded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL display a usable shell (title, example list, empty scope) within 3 seconds on a broadband connection before WASM is fetched.
- WHEN the WASM engine is not yet loaded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show a progress/loading state; it SHALL NOT block rendering of the rest of the UI.
- WHEN rendering a simulation result of ≤ 10 000 points THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL sustain 60 fps on the scope canvas.

---

### 11. Testing

**11.1** As a developer, I need unit tests for the netlist parser and validator so regressions are caught automatically.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that the netlist parser correctly identifies component types, node names, and directive parameters for at least 20 representative netlist lines.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that the validator correctly accepts valid netlists and rejects netlists with: missing ground, floating nodes, unrecognised directives, and malformed component lines.
- WHEN property tests (fast-check) are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify the parser round-trip property: `serialise(parse(netlist)) === normalise(netlist)` for arbitrary well-formed netlists.

**11.2** As a developer, I need a unit test for the result summariser so its numeric outputs are correct.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that summarising a known transient result produces the correct τ, rise time, overshoot, min, max, and final values within ±1% tolerance.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that summarising a known AC result produces the correct –3 dB frequency within ±0.5 dB tolerance.

**11.3** As a developer, I need a unit test for LLM response parsing so malformed model outputs are handled gracefully.

- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that a response containing a fenced code block yields the correct netlist string.
- WHEN unit tests are run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL verify that a response with no fenced block returns a typed parse error rather than throwing.

**11.4** As a developer, I need one end-to-end smoke test so the critical happy path is validated in a real browser.

- WHEN the Playwright smoke test runs THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL: load the app, select the RC low-pass example, wait for the simulation to complete, and assert that a canvas element with a non-blank trace is visible on screen.

</content>
</file>

<content>
# Circuit Séance — Design

**Feature:** Circuit Séance MVP  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** 2026-11-02

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

Circuit Séance is a fully static single-page application. There is no back-end; all computation (WASM simulation, LLM calls) originates in the browser. The architecture is divided into six feature domains that communicate through typed public barrel APIs, a shared library layer (`src/lib/`), and a cross-cutting shared-types layer (`src/shared/`).

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Browser                                                           │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  src/app  — Shell, routing, i18n                             │  │
│  │  ┌────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  │  │
│  │  │  capture   │  │ transcribe  │  │       netlist        │  │  │
│  │  │  feature   │  │  feature    │  │       feature        │  │  │
│  │  └─────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘  │  │
│  │        │                │                     │              │  │
│  │        └────────────────┴─────────────────────┘              │  │
│  │                         │ netlist string                      │  │
│  │              ┌──────────▼──────────┐                         │  │
│  │              │   simulate feature  │◄──── Web Worker         │  │
│  │              │ (useSimulation hook)│      (eecircuit-engine)  │  │
│  │              └──────────┬──────────┘                         │  │
│  │                         │ SimResult                          │  │
│  │           ┌─────────────▼────────────┐                       │  │
│  │           │     scope feature        │                       │  │
│  │           │  (ScopeCanvas + knobs)   │                       │  │
│  │           └─────────────┬────────────┘                       │  │
│  │                         │ compact summary                    │  │
│  │              ┌──────────▼──────────┐                         │  │
│  │              │   spirit feature    │──► LLMAdapter           │  │
│  │              └─────────────────────┘   (openai / anthropic)  │  │
│  │                                                              │  │
│  │  src/lib/llm  — LLMAdapter interface + impls                 │  │
│  │  src/shared   — types, utils, constants                      │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                    │
│  External (user's own key, never project server)                   │
│  ┌──────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────┐                    │
│  │  OpenAI / compat │    │  Anthropic Claude  │                    │
│  └──────────────────┘    └───────────────────┘                    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Web Worker for WASM | ~40 MB WASM + simulation CPU must never jank the UI thread |
| Provider-agnostic `LLMAdapter` | New providers added without touching feature code |
| Barrel-only imports between features | Prevents fragile internal coupling |
| Canvas 2D (not WebGL) | Sufficient for 60 fps at ≤10k points; avoids WebGL context management overhead |
| `sessionStorage` default for API keys | Keys survive page refresh but not browser close; opt-in `localStorage` for persistence |
| Compact summary instead of raw arrays to LLM | Keeps prompt tokens small; avoids exposing raw float arrays that add no pedagogical value |

---

## 2. Component Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "src/app"
        App["App.tsx\n(Shell + layout)"]
        Router["router.tsx"]
        I18n["i18n/en.ts\ni18n/zh-CN.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/capture"
        CapturePanel["CapturePanel.tsx"]
        useCapture["useCapture.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/transcribe"
        TranscribePanel["TranscribePanel.tsx"]
        useTranscribe["useTranscribe.ts"]
        LLMResponseParser["llm-response-parser.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/netlist"
        NetlistEditor["NetlistEditor.tsx\n(CodeMirror 6)"]
        SpiceMode["spice-mode.ts"]
        NetlistParser["netlist-parser.ts"]
        NetlistValidator["netlist-validator.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/simulate"
        useSimulation["useSimulation.ts"]
        SimWorker["sim.worker.ts\n(Web Worker)"]
        ResultSummariser["result-summariser.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/scope"
        ScopeCanvas["ScopeCanvas.tsx"]
        ScopeRenderer["scope-renderer.ts\n(Canvas 2D)"]
        ScopeControls["ScopeControls.tsx\n(knobs, channel select)"]
        PhosphorEffects["phosphor-effects.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "features/spirit"
        SpiritPanel["SpiritPanel.tsx"]
        useSpirit["useSpirit.ts"]
        OfflineExplainer["offline-explainer.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "src/lib/llm"
        LLMAdapter["adapter.ts\n(interface)"]
        OpenAIAdapter["openai.ts"]
        AnthropicAdapter["anthropic.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "src/shared"
        Types["types.ts"]
        Utils["utils.ts"]
    end

    subgraph "src/examples"
        ExampleNets["*.net files"]
    end

    App --> CapturePanel
    App --> TranscribePanel
    App --> NetlistEditor
    App --> ScopeCanvas
    App --> ScopeControls
    App --> SpiritPanel

    useTranscribe --> LLMAdapter
    useTranscribe --> LLMResponseParser
    useSpirit --> LLMAdapter
    useSpirit --> OfflineExplainer

    NetlistEditor --> SpiceMode
    NetlistEditor --> NetlistParser
    NetlistEditor --> NetlistValidator

    useSimulation --> SimWorker
    useSimulation --> ResultSummariser

    ScopeCanvas --> ScopeRenderer
    ScopeRenderer --> PhosphorEffects

    LLMAdapter <|.. OpenAIAdapter
    LLMAdapter <|.. AnthropicAdapter

    useSimulation --> Types
    ScopeRenderer --> Types
    useSpirit --> Types
```

---

## 3. Sequence Diagram — Photo → Netlist → Simulate → Explain

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant CP as CapturePanel
    participant TP as TranscribePanel
    participant NE as NetlistEditor
    participant Val as NetlistValidator
    participant Hook as useSimulation
    participant W as sim.worker.ts (Web Worker)
    participant SC as ScopeCanvas
    participant SP as SpiritPanel
    participant LLM as LLMAdapter (Provider)

    User->>CP: Upload / capture image
    CP->>CP: Compress if > 5 MB
    CP->>TP: imageBase64, mimeType

    User->>TP: Click "Transcribe"
    TP->>LLM: transcribeSchematic(imageBase64, mimeType)
    LLM-->>TP: raw LLM response (markdown + fenced netlist)
    TP->>TP: parseNetlistFromResponse() → netlistText
    TP->>NE: setNetlist(netlistText)
    TP->>Val: validateNetlist(netlistText) [3-stage]
    Val-->>NE: error markers (if any)

    alt Validation passes
        User->>Hook: Click "Simulate" (or auto-triggered)
        Hook->>W: postMessage SimulateRequest {netlist, id}
        W->>W: sim.start() + sim.setNetList()
        W-->>Hook: SimulateProgress {stage: 'running'}
        W->>W: sim.runSim()
        W-->>Hook: SimulateResponse {result: SimResult}
        Hook->>SC: pass SimResult
        SC->>SC: render traces with phosphor effects
        SC-->>User: Animated CRT waveform

        User->>SP: Click "Ask the Spirit"
        SP->>Hook: getCompactSummary(SimResult)
        Hook-->>SP: CompactSummary
        SP->>LLM: explainWaveform(netlist, compactSummary)
        LLM-->>SP: markdown explanation
        SP-->>User: Rendered markdown with "try next" suggestion
    else Validation fails
        Val-->>NE: highlight error lines
        NE-->>User: "Spirits are restless" error panel
    end
```

---

## 4. Data Models / TypeScript Interfaces

All interfaces are defined in `src/shared/types.ts` unless noted.

### 4.1 Simulation types

```ts
// Raw result from eecircuit-engine
interface SimResult {
  header: string;
  numVariables: number;
  variableNames: string[];
  numPoints: number;
  dataType: 'real' | 'complex';
  data: Array<{
    name: string;
    type: string;
    values: number[] | [number, number][]; // real or complex pairs
  }>;
}

type AnalysisType = 'tran' | 'ac' | 'dc' | 'op';

// Compact numeric digest passed to the LLM spirit
interface CompactSummary {
  analysisType: AnalysisType;
  tran?: {
    channels: Array<{
      name: string;
      min: number;
      max: number;
      final: number;
      tauEstimate: number | null;    // 63.2% rise time constant
      riseTime: number | null;       // 10%–90%
      overshootPct: number | null;
    }>;
  };
  ac?: {
    dcGainDb: number;
    minusThreeDbFreq: number | null; // Hz
    peakGainDb: number | null;
    peakFreqHz: number | null;
  };
  dc?: {
    sweepVar: string;
    outputVar: string;
    min: number;
    max: number;
    midSlopePerUnit: number;
  };
  op?: {
    nodeVoltages: Record<string, number>; // node name → volts
  };
}
```

### 4.2 Netlist parsing

```ts
// src/features/netlist/types.ts
type ComponentType =
  | 'R' | 'C' | 'L' | 'V' | 'I'
  | 'D' | 'Q' | 'M' | 'E' | 'F' | 'G' | 'H' | 'X';

interface NetlistComponent {
  type: ComponentType;
  name: string;       // e.g. "R1"
  nodes: string[];    // e.g. ["1", "2"]
  value: string;      // e.g. "10k"
  params: Record<string, string>;
  lineNumber: number;
}

type DirectiveType = 'tran' | 'ac' | 'dc' | 'op' | 'model' | 'subckt' | 'ends' | 'end' | 'other';

interface NetlistDirective {
  type: DirectiveType;
  raw: string;
  lineNumber: number;
}

interface ParsedNetlist {
  title: string;
  components: NetlistComponent[];
  directives: NetlistDirective[];
  errors: ParseError[];
}

interface ParseError {
  lineNumber: number;
  message: string;
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
}
```

### 4.3 Validation

```ts
interface ValidationResult {
  valid: boolean;
  stage: 'syntax' | 'elements' | 'ngspice-dry-run' | 'passed';
  errors: ValidationError[];
}

interface ValidationError {
  lineNumber: number | null;
  message: string;       // human-readable, friendly
  rawMessage: string;    // raw ngspice or parser output
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
}
```

### 4.4 LLM Adapter

```ts
// src/lib/llm/adapter.ts
interface LLMAdapter {
  transcribeSchematic(imageBase64: string, mimeType: string): Promise<string>;
  explainWaveform(
    netlist: string,
    summary: CompactSummary,
    language: 'en' | 'zh-CN',
  ): Promise<string>; // returns markdown
}

interface LLMConfig {
  provider: 'openai' | 'anthropic';
  apiKey: string;
  baseUrl?: string;   // OpenAI-compatible only; default https://api.openai.com/v1
  model?: string;     // override default model
}

class LLMError extends Error {
  provider: 'openai' | 'anthropic';
  statusCode: number;
  // message inherited from Error
}
```

### 4.5 Worker message protocol

```ts
// src/features/simulate/worker-protocol.ts

interface SimulateRequest {
  type: 'simulate';
  id: string;
  netlist: string;
}

interface SimulateResponse {
  type: 'result';
  id: string;
  result: SimResult;
}

interface SimulateError {
  type: 'error';
  id: string;
  message: string;  // friendly message
  raw: string;      // raw ngspice stderr/output
}

interface SimulateProgress {
  type: 'progress';
  id: string;
  stage: 'loading' | 'running';
}

type WorkerInbound = SimulateRequest;
type WorkerOutbound = SimulateResponse | SimulateError | SimulateProgress;
```

### 4.6 Scope display state

```ts
// src/features/scope/types.ts
interface ChannelConfig {
  variableName: string;        // matches SimResult.data[i].name
  color: PhosphorColor;
  voltsPerDiv: number;
  offsetDivisions: number;
  enabled: boolean;
}

type PhosphorColor = 'p31-green' | 'p31-yellow' | 'p31-blue' | 'p31-white';

interface ScopeViewState {
  analysisType: AnalysisType;
  channels: ChannelConfig[];   // up to 4
  timePerDiv: number;          // seconds (tran) | log-decade (ac)
  triggerChannel: number;
  graticule: boolean;
}
```

### 4.7 Application settings (persisted)

```ts
// src/shared/types.ts
interface AppSettings {
  llm: LLMConfig | null;
  storageMode: 'session' | 'local';   // where to persist the API key
  language: 'en' | 'zh-CN';
}
```

---

## 5. Feature Module Details

### 5.1 `features/capture`

- `CapturePanel.tsx` — renders the image preview, "Capture" and "Upload" buttons, and file size warning.
- `useCapture.ts` — manages `File` → `dataURL` → `imageBase64` conversion; client-side compression via Canvas `toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.85)` if size > 5 MB.
- Public API: `{ CapturePanel, useCapture }`, `type { CapturedImage }`.

### 5.2 `features/transcribe`

- `TranscribePanel.tsx` — side-by-side photo / netlist view; "Transcribe" button; confidence note badge.
- `useTranscribe.ts` — calls `LLMAdapter.transcribeSchematic`, owns loading / error state.
- `llm-response-parser.ts` — `parseNetlistFromResponse(raw: string): { netlist: string; note: string } | ParseFailure`. Extracts first fenced block tagged `spice` or plain ` ``` `.
- Public API: `{ TranscribePanel, useTranscribe }`, `type { TranscribeState }`.

### 5.3 `features/netlist`

- `NetlistEditor.tsx` — CodeMirror 6 wrapper; wires spice-mode, linting extensions, error markers.
- `spice-mode.ts` — lezer-based or `StreamLanguage`-based tokeniser for SPICE; tokens: component, directive, model, comment, node, value.
- `netlist-parser.ts` — `parseNetlist(text: string): ParsedNetlist`. Pure function, no side effects.
- `netlist-validator.ts` — `validateNetlist(parsed: ParsedNetlist, dryRun: (nl: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<ValidationResult>`. Three-stage pipeline.
- Public API: `{ NetlistEditor, parseNetlist, validateNetlist }`, `type { ParsedNetlist, ValidationResult }`.

### 5.4 `features/simulate`

- `useSimulation.ts` — React hook that manages a singleton `Worker` reference, request queuing (only one simulation at a time), progress state, and result caching keyed by netlist hash.
- `sim.worker.ts` — Web Worker entry point; lazy-imports `eecircuit-engine`, runs `Simulation`, posts typed messages back.
- `result-summariser.ts` — `summariseResult(result: SimResult, type: AnalysisType): CompactSummary`. Pure function.
- Public API: `{ useSimulation, summariseResult }`, `type { SimResult, CompactSummary, SimulationState }`.

### 5.5 `features/scope`

- `ScopeCanvas.tsx` — React wrapper; owns canvas ref, ResizeObserver, RAF loop, keyboard/touch handler for knobs.
- `scope-renderer.ts` — `ScopeRenderer` class; `draw(state, simResult, timestamp)` called from RAF. Owns off-screen buffer for persistence/afterglow.
- `phosphor-effects.ts` — `applyGlow(ctx, color)`, `applyPersistence(ctx, prev, decay)`, `applyScanlines(ctx)`, `applyFlicker(ctx, timestamp)`. Each is a pure canvas operation, togglable.
- `ScopeControls.tsx` — volts/div knob (scroll wheel + drag), time/div knob, channel enable/color pickers, analysis-type-specific controls.
- Public API: `{ ScopeCanvas, ScopeControls }`, `type { ScopeViewState, ChannelConfig }`.

### 5.6 `features/spirit`

- `SpiritPanel.tsx` — Markdown renderer (via `marked` or `remark`), "Ask the Spirit" button, offline badge.
- `useSpirit.ts` — calls `LLMAdapter.explainWaveform`, tracks loading / error state, falls back to offline explainer.
- `offline-explainer.ts` — `getOfflineExplanation(exampleId: string, summary: CompactSummary): string`. Returns pre-written Markdown keyed by the six example IDs.
- Public API: `{ SpiritPanel, useSpirit }`.

---

## 6. Web Worker Architecture

```
Main Thread                          sim.worker.ts
────────────────────────────────     ───────────────────────────────────
useSimulation                        (lazy import eecircuit-engine)
  ├─ new Worker('./sim.worker.ts')
  │
  ├─ postMessage(SimulateRequest)  →  onmessage: SimulateRequest
  │                                    │
  │  ← SimulateProgress('loading')  ←  postMessage if WASM not yet loaded
  │                                    │  await import('eecircuit-engine')
  │  ← SimulateProgress('running')  ←  sim.start() + sim.setNetList()
  │                                    │  sim.runSim()
  │  ← SimulateResponse             ←  postMessage SimulateResponse
  │    OR SimulateError             ←  catch → postMessage SimulateError
```

The Worker keeps a single `Simulation` instance alive between runs. When a new netlist arrives it calls `sim.setNetList(netlist)` and `sim.runSim()` without re-creating the WASM instance. This avoids the ~200 ms startup cost on every run.

---

## 7. CRT Oscilloscope Rendering

### 7.1 Rendering pipeline (per animation frame)

```
1. Clear back-buffer (with slight alpha < 1 for persistence decay)
2. Draw graticule (10×8 divisions, centre ticks, phosphor tint grid)
3. For each enabled channel:
   a. Project data points into canvas coordinates (volts/div, time/div)
   b. Stroke path with phosphor colour
   c. Apply glow: two radial shadow passes (inner bright, outer dim halo)
4. Copy back-buffer to screen canvas
5. Overlay scanlines (horizontal semi-transparent lines every 2px)
6. Apply flicker: slight global alpha oscillation at ~0.5–2 Hz random walk
7. Draw labels and channel indicators
```

### 7.2 Phosphor colours

| Channel | Base hex | Glow colour |
|---|---|---|
| CH1 | `#39ff14` | `#39ff14` at 40% alpha |
| CH2 | `#aaff44` | `#aaff44` at 35% alpha |
| CH3 | `#ccff88` | `#ccff88` at 30% alpha |
| CH4 | `#e8ffbb` | `#e8ffbb` at 25% alpha |

### 7.3 Persistence / afterglow

The renderer maintains a secondary off-screen canvas (`persistCanvas`). Each frame, `persistCanvas` is drawn to `screenCanvas` with `globalAlpha = 0.85` before the new trace, creating a ~0.5 s natural decay. When `prefers-reduced-motion` is active, `persistCanvas` is not used and each frame fully clears before drawing.

### 7.4 Performance budget

- 10k points × 4 channels = 40k `lineTo` calls per frame.
- Path is batched into a single `beginPath` / `stroke` per channel.
- Glow effect uses `shadowBlur` on context; if frame time exceeds 16 ms for two consecutive frames, glow is automatically reduced in `shadowBlur` radius.

### 7.5 Analysis-type views

| Analysis | X axis | Y axis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.tran` | time (s) | voltage / current | up to 4 channels |
| `.ac` | log₁₀ frequency (Hz) | magnitude (dB) + phase (°) | dual-pane or overlaid |
| `.dc` | sweep variable | output variable | single channel |
| `.op` | — | — | node-voltage table replaces canvas |

---

## 8. LLM Adapter Design

### 8.1 Interface (`src/lib/llm/adapter.ts`)

```ts
interface LLMAdapter {
  transcribeSchematic(imageBase64: string, mimeType: string): Promise<string>;
  explainWaveform(
    netlist: string,
    summary: CompactSummary,
    language: 'en' | 'zh-CN',
  ): Promise<string>;
}
```

### 8.2 OpenAI-compatible adapter

- POST to `${baseUrl}/chat/completions`
- System prompt: instructs model to output exactly one fenced `spice` code block followed by a confidence note.
- Image passed as `{ type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: 'data:{mimeType};base64,{imageBase64}' } }`.
- `explainWaveform` sends netlist + JSON-serialised summary; system prompt requests undergraduate-level explanation + one "try next" suggestion, in the requested language.

### 8.3 Anthropic adapter

- POST to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`
- Image passed as `{ type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type: mimeType, data: imageBase64 } }`.
- Same prompt structure as OpenAI adapter.

### 8.4 LLM response parsing (`features/transcribe/llm-response-parser.ts`)

```
1. Find first occurrence of ```spice or ``` (case-insensitive)
2. Extract content up to closing ```
3. Trim whitespace
4. Look for any text after the closing ``` as the confidence note
5. Return { netlist: string, note: string } | { error: 'no-fence' | 'empty-fence' }
```

---

## 9. i18n Strategy

- String keys are defined once in `src/app/i18n/en.ts` and mirrored in `zh-CN.ts`.
- A lightweight `useTranslation()` hook reads the active locale from `AppSettings.language`.
- No external i18n library is required for the MVP (the string maps are small enough for a plain `Record<string, string>` lookup).
- All user-visible strings — including error messages, ARIA labels, and spirit prompts — must have entries in both locale files.

---

## 10. Error Handling Strategy

| Error source | Handler location | User presentation |
|---|---|---|
| Netlist syntax error | `netlist-validator.ts` | Error markers in editor + validation panel |
| ngspice element/node error | `netlist-validator.ts` | "Spirits are restless" panel, collapsible raw error |
| ngspice runtime error | `sim.worker.ts` → `SimulateError` | Same panel; if pattern recognised → suggest fix |
| LLM network / auth error | `useTranscribe` / `useSpirit` | Toast or inline error message with specific reason |
| LLM response parse failure | `llm-response-parser.ts` → typed error | "Spirit could not read circuit" + manual entry prompt |
| Image too large | `useCapture.ts` | Warning in capture panel; auto-compress |
| Browser unsupported (no File API) | `CapturePanel.tsx` | Static unsupported-feature notice |

All errors must be logged to `console.error` in development mode, and swallowed silently (or shown as friendly messages) in production.

---

## 11. Settings & Key Storage

API keys are stored exclusively in the browser:

- `sessionStorage` (default): key survives page refresh but not browser close.
- `localStorage` (opt-in): key persists across browser sessions; user explicitly enables this.

The key is never included in URLs, query strings, Vite env files, or source code. On the settings UI, the key is masked after entry (`sk-…last4`). The full key is read from storage only at the moment of an LLM request.

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

Circuit Séance is a fully static single-page application. There is no back-end; all computation (WASM simulation, LLM calls) originates in the browser. The architecture is divided into six feature domains that communicate through typed public barrel APIs, a shared library layer (`src/lib/`), and a cross-cutting shared-types layer (`src/shared/`).

### Key design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Web Worker for WASM | ~40 MB WASM + simulation CPU must never jank the UI thread |
| Provider-agnostic `LLMAdapter` | New providers added without touching feature code |
| Barrel-only imports between features | Prevents fragile internal coupling |
| Canvas 2D (not WebGL) | Sufficient for 60 fps at ≤10k points; avoids WebGL context management overhead |
| `sessionStorage` default for API keys | Keys survive page refresh but not browser close; opt-in `localStorage` for persistence |
| Compact summary instead of raw arrays to LLM | Keeps prompt tokens small; avoids exposing raw float arrays that add no pedagogical value |

## 4. Data Models / TypeScript Interfaces

All interfaces are defined in `src/shared/types.ts` unless noted.

### 4.1 Simulation types

```ts

  data: Array<{
    name: string;
    type: string;
    values: number[] | [number, number][]; // real or complex pairs
  }>;
}

type AnalysisType = 'tran' | 'ac' | 'dc' | 'op';

// Compact numeric digest passed to the LLM spirit
interface CompactSummary {
  analysisType: AnalysisType;
  tran?: {
    channels: Array<{
      name: string;
      min: number;
      max: number;
      final: number;
      tauEstimate: number | null;    // 63.2% rise time constant
      riseTime: number | null;       // 10%–90%
      overshootPct: number | null;
    }>;
  };
  ac?: {
    dcGainDb: number;
    minusThreeDbFreq: number | null; // Hz
    peakGainDb: number | null;
    peakFreqHz: number | null;
  };
  dc?: {

    outputVar: string;
    min: number;
    max: number;
    midSlopePerUnit: number;
  };
  op?: {

  };
}
```

### 4.2 Netlist parsing

```ts
// src/features/netlist/types.ts
type ComponentType =
  | 'R' | 'C' | 'L' | 'V' | 'I'
  | 'D' | 'Q' | 'M' | 'E' | 'F' | 'G' | 'H' | 'X';

interface NetlistComponent {
  type: ComponentType;
  name: string;       // e.g. "R1"
  nodes: string[];    // e.g. ["1", "2"]
  value: string;      // e.g. "10k"
  params: Record<string, string>;
  lineNumber: number;
}

type DirectiveType = 'tran' | 'ac' | 'dc' | 'op' | 'model' | 'subckt' | 'ends' | 'end' | 'other';

interface NetlistDirective {
  type: DirectiveType;
  raw: string;
  lineNumber: number;
}

interface ParsedNetlist {
  title: string;
  components: NetlistComponent[];
  directives: NetlistDirective[];
  errors: ParseError[];
}

interface ParseError {
  lineNumber: number;
  message: string;
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
}
```

### 4.3 Validation

```ts
interface ValidationResult {
  valid: boolean;
  stage: 'syntax' | 'elements' | 'ngspice-dry-run' | 'passed';
  errors: ValidationError[];
}

interface ValidationError {
  lineNumber: number | null;
  message: string;       // human-readable, friendly
  rawMessage: string;    // raw ngspice or parser output
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
}
```

### 4.4 LLM Adapter

```ts
// src/lib/llm/adapter.ts
interface LLMAdapter {
  transcribeSchematic(imageBase64: string, mimeType: string): Promise<string>;
  explainWaveform(
    netlist: string,
    summary: CompactSummary,
    language: 'en' | 'zh-CN',
  ): Promise<string>; // returns markdown
}

interface LLMConfig {
  provider: 'openai' | 'anthropic';
  apiKey: string;
  baseUrl?: string;   // OpenAI-compatible only; default https://api.openai.com/v1
  model?: string;     // override default model
}

class LLMError extends Error {
  provider: 'openai' | 'anthropic';
  statusCode: number;
  // message inherited from Error
}
```

### 4.5 Worker message protocol

```ts
// src/features/simulate/worker-protocol.ts

interface SimulateRequest {
  type: 'simulate';
  id: string;
  netlist: string;
}

interface SimulateResponse {
  type: 'result';
  id: string;
  result: SimResult;
}

interface SimulateError {
  type: 'error';
  id: string;
  message: string;  // friendly message
  raw: string;      // raw ngspice stderr/output
}

interface SimulateProgress {
  type: 'progress';
  id: string;
  stage: 'loading' | 'running';
}

type WorkerInbound = SimulateRequest;
type WorkerOutbound = SimulateResponse | SimulateError | SimulateProgress;
```

### 4.6 Scope display state

```ts
// src/features/scope/types.ts
interface ChannelConfig {
  variableName: string;        // matches SimResult.data[i].name
  color: PhosphorColor;
  voltsPerDiv: number;
  offsetDivisions: number;
  enabled: boolean;
}

type PhosphorColor = 'p31-green' | 'p31-yellow' | 'p31-blue' | 'p31-white';

interface ScopeViewState {
  analysisType: AnalysisType;
  channels: ChannelConfig[];   // up to 4
  timePerDiv: number;          // seconds (tran) | log-decade (ac)
  triggerChannel: number;
  graticule: boolean;
}
```

### 4.7 Application settings (persisted)

```ts
// src/shared/types.ts
interface AppSettings {
  llm: LLMConfig | null;
  storageMode: 'session' | 'local';   // where to persist the API key
  language: 'en' | 'zh-CN';
}
```

---

## 5. Feature Module Details

### 5.1 `features/capture`

- `CapturePanel.tsx` — renders the image preview, "Capture" and "Upload" buttons, and file size warning.
- `useCapture.ts` — manages `File` → `dataURL` → `imageBase64` conversion; client-side compression via Canvas `toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.85)` if size > 5 MB.
- Public API: `{ CapturePanel, useCapture }`, `type { CapturedImage }`.

### 5.2 `features/transcribe`

- `TranscribePanel.tsx` — side-by-side photo / netlist view; "Transcribe" button; confidence note badge.
- `useTranscribe.ts` — calls `LLMAdapter.transcribeSchematic`, owns loading / error state.
- `llm-response-parser.ts` — `parseNetlistFromResponse(raw: string): { netlist: string; note: string } | ParseFailure`. Extracts first fenced block tagged `spice` or plain ` ``` `.
- Public API: `{ TranscribePanel, useTranscribe }`, `type { TranscribeState }`.

### 5.3 `features/netlist`

- `NetlistEditor.tsx` — CodeMirror 6 wrapper; wires spice-mode, linting extensions, error markers.
- `spice-mode.ts` — lezer-based or `StreamLanguage`-based tokeniser for SPICE; tokens: component, directive, model, comment, node, value.
- `netlist-parser.ts` — `parseNetlist(text: string): ParsedNetlist`. Pure function, no side effects.
- `netlist-validator.ts` — `validateNetlist(parsed: ParsedNetlist, dryRun: (nl: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<ValidationResult>`. Three-stage pipeline.
- Public API: `{ NetlistEditor, parseNetlist, validateNetlist }`, `type { ParsedNetlist, ValidationResult }`.

### 5.4 `features/simulate`

- `useSimulation.ts` — React hook that manages a singleton `Worker` reference, request queuing (only one simulation at a time), progress state, and result caching keyed by netlist hash.
- `sim.worker.ts` — Web Worker entry point; lazy-imports `eecircuit-engine`, runs `Simulation`, posts typed messages back.
- `result-summariser.ts` — `summariseResult(result: SimResult, type: AnalysisType): CompactSummary`. Pure function.
- Public API: `{ useSimulation, summariseResult }`, `type { SimResult, CompactSummary, SimulationState }`.

### 5.5 `features/scope`

- `ScopeCanvas.tsx` — React wrapper; owns canvas ref, ResizeObserver, RAF loop, keyboard/touch handler for knobs.
- `scope-renderer.ts` — `ScopeRenderer` class; `draw(state, simResult, timestamp)` called from RAF. Owns off-screen buffer for persistence/afterglow.
- `phosphor-effects.ts` — `applyGlow(ctx, color)`, `applyPersistence(ctx, prev, decay)`, `applyScanlines(ctx)`, `applyFlicker(ctx, timestamp)`. Each is a pure canvas operation, togglable.
- `ScopeControls.tsx` — volts/div knob (scroll wheel + drag), time/div knob, channel enable/color pickers, analysis-type-specific controls.
- Public API: `{ ScopeCanvas, ScopeControls }`, `type { ScopeViewState, ChannelConfig }`.

### 5.6 `features/spirit`

- `SpiritPanel.tsx` — Markdown renderer (via `marked` or `remark`), "Ask the Spirit" button, offline badge.
- `useSpirit.ts` — calls `LLMAdapter.explainWaveform`, tracks loading / error state, falls back to offline explainer.
- `offline-explainer.ts` — `getOfflineExplanation(exampleId: string, summary: CompactSummary): string`. Returns pre-written Markdown keyed by the six example IDs.
- Public API: `{ SpiritPanel, useSpirit }`.

---

## 6. Web Worker Architecture

```
Main Thread                          sim.worker.ts
────────────────────────────────     ───────────────────────────────────
useSimulation                        (lazy import eecircuit-engine)
  ├─ new Worker('./sim.worker.ts')
  │
  ├─ postMessage(SimulateRequest)  →  onmessage: SimulateRequest
  │                                    │
  │  ← SimulateProgress('loading')  ←  postMessage if WASM not yet loaded
  │                                    │  await import('eecircuit-engine')
  │  ← SimulateProgress('running')  ←  sim.start() + sim.setNetList()
  │                                    │  sim.runSim()
  │  ← SimulateResponse             ←  postMessage SimulateResponse
  │    OR SimulateError             ←  catch → postMessage SimulateError
```

The Worker keeps a single `Simulation` instance alive between runs. When a new netlist arrives it calls `sim.setNetList(netlist)` and `sim.runSim()` without re-creating the WASM instance. This avoids the ~200 ms startup cost on every run.

---

## 7. CRT Oscilloscope Rendering

### 7.1 Rendering pipeline (per animation frame)

```
1. Clear back-buffer (with slight alpha < 1 for persistence decay)
2. Draw graticule (10×8 divisions, centre ticks, phosphor tint grid)
3. For each enabled channel:
   a. Project data points into canvas coordinates (volts/div, time/div)
   b. Stroke path with phosphor colour
   c. Apply glow: two radial shadow passes (inner bright, outer dim halo)
4. Copy back-buffer to screen canvas
5. Overlay scanlines (horizontal semi-transparent lines every 2px)
6. Apply flicker: slight global alpha oscillation at ~0.5–2 Hz random walk
7. Draw labels and channel indicators
```

### 7.2 Phosphor colours

| Channel | Base hex | Glow colour |
|---|---|---|
| CH1 | `#39ff14` | `#39ff14` at 40% alpha |
| CH2 | `#aaff44` | `#aaff44` at 35% alpha |
| CH3 | `#ccff88` | `#ccff88` at 30% alpha |
| CH4 | `#e8ffbb` | `#e8ffbb` at 25% alpha |

### 7.3 Persistence / afterglow

The renderer maintains a secondary off-screen canvas (`persistCanvas`). Each frame, `persistCanvas` is drawn to `screenCanvas` with `globalAlpha = 0.85` before the new trace, creating a ~0.5 s natural decay. When `prefers-reduced-motion` is active, `persistCanvas` is not used and each frame fully clears before drawing.

### 7.4 Performance budget

- 10k points × 4 channels = 40k `lineTo` calls per frame.
- Path is batched into a single `beginPath` / `stroke` per channel.
- Glow effect uses `shadowBlur` on context; if frame time exceeds 16 ms for two consecutive frames, glow is automatically reduced in `shadowBlur` radius.

### 7.5 Analysis-type views

| Analysis | X axis | Y axis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.tran` | time (s) | voltage / current | up to 4 channels |
| `.ac` | log₁₀ frequency (Hz) | magnitude (dB) + phase (°) | dual-pane or overlaid |
| `.dc` | sweep variable | output variable | single channel |
| `.op` | — | — | node-voltage table replaces canvas |

---

## 8. LLM Adapter Design

### 8.1 Interface (`src/lib/llm/adapter.ts`)

```ts
interface LLMAdapter {
  transcribeSchematic(imageBase64: string, mimeType: string): Promise<string>;
  explainWaveform(
    netlist: string,
    summary: CompactSummary,
    language: 'en' | 'zh-CN',
  ): Promise<string>;
}
```

### 8.2 OpenAI-compatible adapter

- POST to `${baseUrl}/chat/completions`
- System prompt: instructs model to output exactly one fenced `spice` code block followed by a confidence note.
- Image passed as `{ type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: 'data:{mimeType};base64,{imageBase64}' } }`.
- `explainWaveform` sends netlist + JSON-serialised summary; system prompt requests undergraduate-level explanation + one "try next" suggestion, in the requested language.

### 8.3 Anthropic adapter

- POST to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`
- Image passed as `{ type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type: mimeType, data: imageBase64 } }`.
- Same prompt structure as OpenAI adapter.

### 8.4 LLM response parsing (`features/transcribe/llm-response-parser.ts`)

```
1. Find first occurrence of ```spice or ``` (case-insensitive)
2. Extract content up to closing ```
3. Trim whitespace
4. Look for any text after the closing ``` as the confidence note
5. Return { netlist: string, note: string } | { error: 'no-fence' | 'empty-fence' }
```

---

## 9. i18n Strategy

- String keys are defined once in `src/app/i18n/en.ts` and mirrored in `zh-CN.ts`.
- A lightweight `useTranslation()` hook reads the active locale from `AppSettings.language`.
- No external i18n library is required for the MVP (the string maps are small enough for a plain `Record<string, string>` lookup).
- All user-visible strings — including error messages, ARIA labels, and spirit prompts — must have entries in both locale files.

---

## 10. Error Handling Strategy

| Error source | Handler location | User presentation |
|---|---|---|
| Netlist syntax error | `netlist-validator.ts` | Error markers in editor + validation panel |
| ngspice element/node error | `netlist-validator.ts` | "Spirits are restless" panel, collapsible raw error |
| ngspice runtime error | `sim.worker.ts` → `SimulateError` | Same panel; if pattern recognised → suggest fix |
| LLM network / auth error | `useTranscribe` / `useSpirit` | Toast or inline error message with specific reason |
| LLM response parse failure | `llm-response-parser.ts` → typed error | "Spirit could not read circuit" + manual entry prompt |
| Image too large | `useCapture.ts` | Warning in capture panel; auto-compress |
| Browser unsupported (no File API) | `CapturePanel.tsx` | Static unsupported-feature notice |

All errors must be logged to `console.error` in development mode, and swallowed silently (or shown as friendly messages) in production.

---

## 11. Settings & Key Storage

API keys are stored exclusively in the browser:

- `sessionStorage` (default): key survives page refresh but not browser close.
- `localStorage` (opt-in): key persists across browser sessions; user explicitly enables this.

The key is never included in URLs, query strings, Vite env files, or source code. On the settings UI, the key is masked after entry (`sk-…last4`). The full key is read from storage only at the moment of an LLM request.

---

## 12. Folder / File Checklist

```
src/
├── app/
│   ├── App.tsx
│   ├── router.tsx

---

## 13. Testing Strategy

### Unit tests (Vitest)

| File | Coverage target |
|---|---|
| `netlist-parser.test.ts` | ≥ 20 representative lines; component types, node names, directives, comments |
| `netlist-parser.property.test.ts` | fast-check: `serialise(parse(nl)) === normalise(nl)` for well-formed inputs |
| `netlist-validator.test.ts` | accepts valid; rejects missing-ground, floating nodes, bad directives |
| `result-summariser.test.ts` | τ, rise-time, overshoot, –3 dB freq against known fixtures |
| `llm-response-parser.test.ts` | fenced-block extraction, no-fence error, empty-fence error |

### End-to-end (Playwright)

`smoke.spec.ts`:
1. Navigate to `http://localhost:5173`.
2. Click the RC low-pass example.
3. Wait for `[data-testid="scope-canvas"]` to be visible and for `[data-testid="sim-status"]` to contain "complete".
4. Assert the canvas `data-has-trace="true"` attribute is set (set by the renderer after first draw).

### CI requirements

- `npm test` (Vitest single-run) must pass before merge.
- `npm run lint` must pass before merge.
- Playwright smoke test runs in CI on the built bundle (`npm run build && npx playwright test`).

Implement the spirit panel _Requirements: 8.1, 8.2, 8.3_ - [ ] 17.1 Create `src/features/spirit/use-spirit.ts` hook: accepts `LLMAdapter | null`, `netlist`, `summary`, `exampleId | null`, `language`; exposes `explain()`, `state`, `explanation: string | null`; falls back to `getOfflineExplanation` when `adapter` is null and `exampleId` is set; adds "offline mode" flag to state. - [ ] 17.2 Install `marked` (or `remark` + `rehype`) for Markdown rendering; pin exact version. - [ ] 17.3 Create `src/features/spirit/SpiritPanel.tsx`: renders explanation Markdown in a styled panel with CRT-inspired typography (monospace, green tint); shows "Ask the Spirit" button; shows offline badge when applicable; shows loading skeleton during fetch; shows error message with retry on failure. --- ## Phase 9 — Integration & Wiring - [ ] 18. Wire all features together in App.tsx _Requirements: 9.1, 9.2_ - [ ] 18.1 Connect `useCapture` → `TranscribePanel` → `NetlistEditor` data flow: captured image flows to transcribe; transcribed netlist flows to editor. - [ ] 18.2 Connect `NetlistEditor` → `useSimulation` → `ScopeCanvas` data flow: on "Simulate" click (or example load), run validation then simulation; pass `SimResult` to scope. - [ ] 18.3 Connect `useSimulation` → `summariseResult` → `useSpirit` data flow: after simulation completes, compute summary; pass to spirit hook. - [ ] 18.4 Wire example selector: clicking an example sets the netlist in the editor, sets `exampleId`, and auto-triggers simulation. - [ ] 18.5 Wire language toggle to `LanguageContext` and propagate to LLM adapter calls. - [ ] 18.6 Wire settings panel to `createAdapter(config)`: when config changes, recreate the adapter and pass to `useTranscribe` and `useSpirit`. - [ ] 18.7 Ensure the "Simulate" button is disabled when validation has errors; "Transcribe" and "Ask Spirit" buttons are disabled when no API key is configured. - [ ] 19. Mobile & responsive polish _Requirements: 5.3, 9.1_ - [ ] 19.1 Verify the capture flow on a mobile-viewport layout (375 × 667 px): all buttons reachable, camera input works, scope readable in landscape. - [ ] 19.2 Add a CSS media query for `(orientation: landscape) and (max-width: 767px)`: scope canvas full-width, controls below. - [ ] 19.3 Verify touch targets ≥ 44 × 44 px on all primary controls; add `min-height`/`min-width` CSS where needed. --- ## Phase 10 — Accessibility & Performance - [ ] 20. Accessibility pass _Requirements: 10.1_ - [ ] 20.1 Add `aria-label` to all icon-only buttons (settings gear, language toggle, close button, Transcribe, Ask Spirit, Simulate). - [ ] 20.2 Verify keyboard tab order through the primary controls (example list → editor → simulate button → scope controls → ask spirit button → settings). - [ ] 20.3 Verify WCAG AA contrast (≥ 4.5:1) for all text labels, axis labels, and status messages over the dark CRT background; adjust colours as needed. - [ ] 20.4 Implement `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in `scope-renderer.ts` and `phosphor-effects.ts`: disable flicker, scanlines animation, and persistence trail; keep static glow. - [ ] 21. Performance optimisation _Requirements: 4.1, 10.2_ - [ ] 21.1 Verify the WASM package is fetched only once and cached by the browser (confirm `Cache-Control` headers in Vite build output; add `vite-plugin-pwa` or manual service worker if needed for offline WASM caching). - [ ] 21.2 Add a "Summoning…" spinner / progress bar to the scope area that appears immediately on page load while WASM is being fetched; confirm the rest of the UI (example list, editor) renders before WASM finishes loading. - [ ] 21.3 Profile the scope RAF loop with 10k points × 4 channels; verify ≥ 60 fps on Chrome on a mid-range machine; apply path batching or offscreen canvas if needed. --- ## Phase 11 — Tests - [ ] 22. Unit tests — result summariser _Requirements: 11.2_ - [ ] 23.1 Create `tests/fixtures/sim-results/` with at least two fixture JSON files: one RC transient result (known τ, rise time) and one RLC AC result (known –3 dB frequency). - [ ] 23.2 Create `tests/unit/features/simulate/result-summariser.test.ts`; verify τ within ±1%, rise time within ±1%, overshoot within ±1% against RC transient fixture; verify –3 dB frequency within ±0.5 dB against AC fixture. - [ ] 24. Copy and flavour text _Requirements: 1.2, 9.1_ - [ ] 26.1 Review all i18n strings for the "Resurrection" / haunted tone: "Summoning the spirits…", "The spirits are restless", "Ask the Spirit", "电路招魂", etc.; ensure English and Chinese versions are both present. - [ ] 26.2 Add a brief hero tagline to the top toolbar or a splash overlay on first load: "Berkeley SPICE, resurrected in your browser." - [ ] 27. Production build verification _Requirements: 9.2_ - [ ] 27.1 Run `npm run build`; confirm `dist/` contains only static files; confirm no TypeScript errors; confirm no ESLint errors. - [ ] 27.2 Serve `dist/` locally (`npx serve dist`) and manually smoke-test the RC example end-to-end in Chrome and Firefox. - [ ] 27.3 Verify the WASM binary is included in `dist/` and loads correctly from the static origin (no CORS issues). - [ ] 27.4 Add a `public/` favicon (CRT green oscilloscope icon or a ghost icon) and update `index.html` `` to "Circuit Séance — 电路招魂". </content> </file>
